sections.OPEN QUESTIONS:
1) What is the average return period of this Source? The catalogue (CPTI, 2004), spanning about 1000 years, reports only the 1570 earthquake that can be associated with the outermost part of the Ferrara Arc.
2) What is the seismic behaviour of this Source? The length of the mapped blind thrust exceeds that of the Ferrara Source. Did the remaining parts already rupture?
sections.SUMMARIES:
Although no specific studies exist on this Source, information about the location, geometry and activity of the source, possible causative fault of the Me 5.5 1570 Ferrara earthquake, can be retrieved from several papers regarding the recent activity of the Ferrara Folds and from subsurface geology.
Pieri and Groppi (1981)
This paper offers a reconstruction of the subsurface geology of the Po Plain using data derived from exploratory seismic lines and oil wells stratigraphies. Their NE-oriented section 10 shows the presence of an anticline beneath Ferrara deforms sediments as recent as middle-upper Pliocene. This anticline is driven by one of the outermost thrusts of the Ferrara Arc.
Veggiani (1985)
This author reconstructs the idrographic evolution of the eastern portion of the Po Plain during the last 3000 years, through geomorphological, archaeological and historical researches.
This study relates the changes in the idrography of this area to climatic events, subsidence due to sediments compaction and tectonic movements along the Ferrara Arc. In particular, it relates to tectonic movements the shift to the north and the union of two branches of the Po river occurred between the 9th and the 8th century b.C. Also the definitive abandonment of the southern courses of the Po river in the 12th century is related to tectonic activity of the Ferrara Arc.
Boschi et al. (2000)
This catalogue describes some effects on the environment widespread around the epicentral area of the 1570 earthquake. At Ferrara various liquefaction phenomena were observed, together with an increase of the water level in the castle trench. At Belriguardo a fracture in the ground with emission of hot gasses is reported and at Stellata the flow of the Po river stopped and subsequently the level of the river increased and suddenly decreased.
Prestininzi and Romeo (2000)
This catalogue reports various liquefaction effects and topographic changes at and around Ferrara. Liquefaction phenomena are described also at Ficarolo and Giara del Po, while at Belriguardo a fracture with gas emission is reported.
Burrato et al. (2003)
These authors provide an inventory of the river anomalies of the Po Plain with wave-lengths comparable to that of tectonic structures of crustal significance and suggestive of the presence of active blind thrust or reverse faults. As second step, the authors compare the position of the drainage anomalies with the location of known buried anticlines, to corroborate the hypothesis of the tectonic nature of the anomalies. They report a diversion of the Po river at Ficarolo and the presence of abandoned channels south of its present position, and the abrupt diversion toward the East of the Reno river at S. Agostino, both associated with buried anticlines belonging to the Ferrara Folds.
Boccaletti and Martelli (2004)
This map defines as active the structures of the Ferrara Arc, based on both the analysis of seismic reflection profiles and field data. According to these, the base of the alluvial deposits of the Po Plain (dated younger than 450 ka) is affected by tectonic deformations at various localities along the Ferrara Folds. In particular, its section C-C' shows the presence of a blind thrust few kilometres NW of Ferrara affecting Middle Pleistocene Holocene deposits and driving a shallow anticline deforming the top of the Upper Pliocene sequence.
Moreover this map shows that the deposits of the Apennine rivers do not reach the Po River and do not go beyond the high of the Ferrara Folds. The course of the Po river is shifted toward the North where the front of the Ferrara Folds is shallower.
Rovida (2004)
The author analyses the effects on the environment produced by historical earthquakes occurred in the Po Plain, and investigates in detail a selection of the largest events in order to assess their seismogenic sources. He first compares the sources derived from macroseismic data alone using the Boxer code (Gasperini et al., 1999), with the mapped active structures buried in the Po Plain. Then, to constrain better their geometry, he studies in detail the geomorphic expression of these sources using elastic dislocation models and geomorphological observations. As a final results the author proposes 11 new seismogenic sources, responsible for M 5+ and higher earthquakes in the Po Plain.

pictures.c: Recent evolution of the Po River and its main tributaries. The thrust fault driving the Mirandola anticline is likely responsible for the attraction of the Panaro and Secchia rivers towards the syncline north of Modena, while the Po River appears to be shifted northward (from Veggiani [1985]).
